result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A carries one idea, the flat as the way in plus a 64-of-100 wheel, through all four pieces, sticks to the fact sheet, and adds ask-the-owner lines and a plain fallback for the board. B is well shaped for each format, and its email has a subject line, preview text and a sign-up button, but it adds unsupported claims ('most people who ride have had a flat,' bikes 'leaning in a hallway'). It also offers no fallback concept. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers build on the flat-tire fact and stay close to the fact sheet. B is stronger: its 100-spoke wheel ties all four pieces together and plays on the Spoke Yard name. B also flags its assumption that beginners feel nervous, uses clear placeholders and ask-the-owner lines, and gives a fallback concept. A has no fallback and adds a small invented detail (bikes 'leaning in a hallway').
